user.title: SecuraCV Setup
user.description: Choose how to connect to your SecuraCV devices. Automatic is right for almost everyone: it detects what's installed and configures itself with no further questions.

data_description.setup_mode: Automatic probes for a running Privacy Witness Kernel and enables MQTT for Canary devices. Pick a manual mode only if you need a non-default URL or topic prefix.

confirm.title: Add SecuraCV
confirm.description: Canary devices are publishing on the MQTT prefix `{prefix}`. Nothing else is needed — submit to add them to Home Assistant.

hassio_confirm.title: Add SecuraCV
hassio_confirm.description: The Privacy Witness Kernel add-on announced itself at {url}. Submit to connect to it and enable MQTT discovery for Canary devices — nothing else is needed.

mqtt_config.title: MQTT Configuration
mqtt_config.description:
Configure MQTT for Canary device auto-discovery.

Canary devices publish to topics under this prefix. Devices will appear automatically in Home Assistant.

data_description.mqtt_prefix: MQTT topic prefix for Canary devices (default: securacv)

kernel.title: Witness Kernel Connection
kernel.description:
Enter the connection details for your SecuraCV Privacy Witness Kernel.

The kernel runs as a Home Assistant app, Docker container, or standalone service. The kernel rotates its API token every 10 minutes, so prefer the token file (the app writes it to /config/api_token); use a static token only for kernels whose token file Home Assistant cannot read.

data_description.url: URL of the Privacy Witness Kernel Event API (e.g., http://d0491a67-privacy-witness-kernel:8799 for the add-on)
data_description.token_file: Path to the kernel's rotating token file; re-read automatically when the token rotates (default: /config/api_token)
data_description.token: Bearer token pasted from the kernel's api_token file — goes stale within 10 minutes unless a token file is also set
data_description.adapter_stats_url: Read-only adapter_host stats endpoint, e.g. http://adapter-host:8799 — surfaces per-adapter health as a diagnostic sensor.

both.title: MQTT + Kernel Connection
both.description: Configure both MQTT for Canary devices and HTTP for the Witness Kernel. The kernel rotates its API token every 10 minutes, so prefer the token file (the app writes it to /config/api_token).

data_description.url: URL of the Privacy Witness Kernel Event API
data_description.token_file: Path to the kernel's rotating token file; re-read automatically when the token rotates (default: /config/api_token)
data_description.token: Bearer token pasted from the kernel's api_token file — goes stale within 10 minutes unless a token file is also set
data_description.mqtt_prefix: MQTT topic prefix for Canary devices (default: securacv)
data_description.adapter_stats_url: Read-only adapter_host stats endpoint, e.g. http://adapter-host:8799 — surfaces per-adapter health as a diagnostic sensor.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot connect to the Privacy Witness Kernel. Check the URL and ensure the kernel is running.
error.invalid_auth: Invalid API token. Check the token file path, or re-read the token from the kernel's api_token file.
error.token_required: Provide an API token file path or a static token (the token file is recommended — the kernel rotates the token every 10 minutes).

abort.already_configured: This SecuraCV system is already configured.
abort.invalid_discovery_info: The discovery announcement was missing its connection details (host and port).

mqtt_subscribe_failed.title: SecuraCV can't subscribe to MQTT

init.title: Device key management
init.description: Pin, rotate, or unpin a Canary device's Ed25519 public key. Read the key off the device, not over MQTT: a canary-wap shows it on its /enroll page, and the firmware/canary build and canary-vision print it on USB serial (`j`). A canary-sense or canary-sentinel shows only its fingerprint, in its boot log, so compare that with the pinned_fingerprint attribute instead of pinning by hand. A canary-display has no key to pin.

pin.title: Pin device pubkey
pin.description: Paste the device_id and the full 64-character Ed25519 pubkey hex, read off the device: the /enroll page on a canary-wap, or the USB serial `j` output on the firmware/canary build or canary-vision.

rotate.title: Rotate pinned key
rotate.description: Replace the existing pin with a new pubkey. The previous key is retained in the audit trail. The mismatch notification for this device (if any) is cleared.

unpin.title: Unpin device
unpin.description: Drop the device's pin. The next publish will TOFU-pin to whatever pubkey arrives.

error.invalid_pubkey_hex: Public key must be exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.
error.device_not_pinned: No pin exists for this device_id.
error.trust_store_unavailable: The trust store isn't loaded for this entry — try reloading the integration.

no_loaded_entry.message: SecuraCV has no loaded entry, so nothing is running its watches. Enable or reload the integration to use them.

watches_unreadable.message: SecuraCV could not read its stored watches (the log has the reason), so its watches are not available. Reload the integration to try again.

not_loaded_yet.message: SecuraCV is not loaded yet, so its watches are not available. Try again once the integration has started.

duration_unreadable.message: Can't tell how long {duration} is. Give it in days, weeks, months, seasons or years ("two weeks", "10 days"), or leave it out for {default_days} days.

subject_empty.message: Say what to keep an eye on: subject is empty.

watch_limit_reached.message: Already running {count} watches, which is as many as the hub keeps. End one with securacv.end_watch first.

watch_ref_empty.message: Say which watch to end: its id or its label.

watch_not_found.message: No watch is called {watch}. securacv.list_watches names the ones running.

watch_ambiguous.message: {watch} names {count} watches ({ids}); end it by id.

start_watch.name: Start a watch
start_watch.description: Starts a bounded, self-expiring watch on something the fleet already senses. Adds attention only: it cannot arm, disarm or unseal anything, and it never turns on new sensing. Returns the watch, including the id that End a watch takes.

subject.name: Subject
subject.description: What to keep an eye on, the way you would say it. A Canary's name binds the watch to that device's witness events; anything else is accepted but stays unfed until something in the fleet reports it.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How long, in days, weeks, months, seasons or years: "two weeks", "10 days", "a month". A duration with none of those units ("48 hours") is refused, not guessed. 14 days if left out; never longer than a year.

concern.name: Concern
concern.description: What to tell you about. Left out, it is read off the subject's wording ("if it stops reporting"), or it is "if anything changes".

end_watch.name: End a watch
end_watch.description: Ends a watch early and removes it. Name it by its id (from Start a watch or List watches) or by its label; a label two watches share is refused rather than guessed. The early end is announced like an expiry. Returns the watch as it ended.

watch.name: Watch
watch.description: The watch's id, or its label as you said it.

list_watches.name: List watches
list_watches.description: Returns the watches currently running, each with its state, what it is bound to and how many days it has left. Response only.
